ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on any person listed as Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by Law No. 80 of 2002 and its executive regulations. Compulsory real-time screening against consolidated Egyptian domestic sanctions lists, UN Security Council sanctions resolutions, OFAC SDN List, EU consolidated list, and FATF public statements. Ongoing negative media and adverse information check; continuous transaction monitoring and re-verification of UBO status at least annually or upon any ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) online services portal (Investor Services portal at https://www.invest-in-egypt.com / GAFI electronic company registration)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names in mainland Egypt must be in Arabic script, with an optional Latin transliteration for foreign purposes. The Arabic name must be phonetically transliterated to match the approved foreign name. Commercial slogans or trademarks may require additional protection registration. All names must comply with Law No. 159 of 1981 (Companies Law) and the Commercial Code.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant shall submit a formal written appeal to the GAFI Commercial Registration Dispute Unit within 30 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include the proposed name, the rejection ground, legal arguments, and any supplementary trademark or consent letters. The applicant may alternatively file a revised name application through the GAFI portal without prejudice to the appeal. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may challenge the decision before the Administrative Court of the State Council under Article 24 of the State Council Law (Law No. 47 of 1972, as amended).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable for the intended construction sector. Egypt requires a physical registered office within the relevant governorate (typically required for service of legal notices, attendance of labor inspections, and registration with the General Organization for Social Insurance). A virtual or temporary office is not recognized as a compliant registered office for an LLC engaged in geotechnical foundation contracting due to physical construction sites and machine registration needs.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High for ISIC 4390 contracting activity. GAFI, the Commercial Registry, the Labor Inspectorate, the Tax Authority, and the Civil Defense Authority each retain the right of unannounced physical on-site inspection. The probability of at least one such inspection within the first 12 months of active operation is conservatively assessed at 75% due to involvement with deep excavation, underground structures, and heavy equipment that trigger municipal licensing and labor safety checks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018), Articles 20-24 and 221; Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 96 of 1982; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Commercial Registry Department, Ministry of Trade and Industry
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Statute of the LLC) submitted through the GAFI All-in-One electronic corporate formation portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum paid-up capital of EGP 50,000, fully subscribed and deposited in a licensed Egyptian bank in a company-name temporary account; the bank's capital deposit certificate must be submitted at incorporation. No separate escrow account is required beyond this deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporators and subscribers, having signed the Statutory Memorandum of Association, hereby ratify the subscription of shares in the Company as set out in Schedule 1. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company shall be established at [Address], Cairo Governorate, where statutory records shall be maintained. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] of [Nationality] be and is hereby appointed as Managing Manager, and [Name] as Company Secretary, each authorized to execute banking instructions, sign employment contracts, and represent the Company before the Commercial Registry, tax authorities, and all licensing bodies. RESOLVED FINALLY, that the officers shall file all declarations required to obtain operational permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Legal Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (Online Corporate Formation Portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the GAFI electronic platform, submit a legal clearance application for the proposed LLC name, select the activity code ISIC 4390 (deep foundation and diaphragm wall works), pay the name reservation fee, and download the electronic name clearance certificate.
required_dossiers: Copy of each shareholder's ID or passport
Power of attorney if using an authorized local representative
Three proposed company names (primary plus two alternates)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity or prohibited marks, the applicant may immediately submit any of the listed alternate names; the first two alternates are processed without an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Licensed Commercial Bank in Egypt (e.g., National Bank of Egypt, Banque Misr, or majority-owned subsidiary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary company capital account using the reserved trade name; deposit the minimum paid-up capital of EGP 50,000 from a lawful source; obtain an official capital deposit certificate (Shahadat Al-Qayd) confirming the balance and accounting for each shareholder's contribution.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Copies of shareholders' passports or national IDs
Initial board resolution authorizing the bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank identifies a mismatch between shareholder names in the passport and the draft memorandum, obtain a corrected memorandum through a supplementary notarial deed and re-present the certificate to the bank for endorsement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Notary Public – General Authority for Notarization, Ministry of Justice
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the final Arabic version of the LLC contract (Memorandum and Articles) incorporating the bank deposit certificate and registered office address; all founding shareholders or their legal attorneys must personally appear before the notary for signature authentication; the notary will seal every page after verifying the legal clauses and the supervisory approval from GAFI.
required_dossiers: Founding shareholders' original passports or national IDs
Lease contract or title deed for the registered office
List of managers and their signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies missing statutory clauses, instruct counsel to draft a supplementary deed, execute it before the same notary, and re-submit the complete document package for notarial stamping within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Approval and Commercial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – All-in-One Corporate Registration Window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association, capital deposit certificate, lease agreement, and the pro-forma board resolution to the GAFI platform; pay the official filing fee; undergo legal review; upon approval, GAFI will create the Commercial Registration entry and issue the company's incorporation certificate, tax card, and organizational ID number.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association (original)
Valid lease contract for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI sends a query regarding the registered office or capital verification, respond via the portal within 10 days with corrected lease or supplementary notarial documentation; the filing will be reinstated without a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and the National Social Insurance Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the LLC's commercial registration and tax card issued under step 4, file the tax declaration with ETA to obtain a permanent tax identification number and VAT registration; simultaneously register the company with the Social Insurance Authority for employee mandatory insurance purposes; obtain the establishment certificate and allocate a social insurance file number.
required_dossiers: Bank account statements for payroll (if requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of delay or query from the Tax Authority regarding classification of activities, present the ISIC 4390 certificate and contractual references to geotechnical works, and request a fast-track reassessment under the Large Taxpayer Services division.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Egyptian Federation for Construction and Building Contractors (EFCBC) – Classification Committee, Ministry of Housing, Utilities and Urban Development
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Construction Contractor Classification Certificate – Grade A, Specialized Geotechnical Works (Deep Slurry Trenching and Diaphragm Wall Installation)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Central Department for Environmental Impact Assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Limited Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA Form B) requiring submission of an Environmental Management Plan (EMP) and periodic self-monitoring reports to the EEAA regional office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with Law No. 4 of 1994 (amended by Law No. 9 of 2009): treated wastewater pH 6-9, total suspended solids ≤ 60 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 15 mg/L; trenching slurry and bentonite waste shall be dewatered and transported to an approved landfill; diesel generator emissions limited to particulate matter PM10 ≤ 100 µg/m³; site boundary noise levels ≤ 65 dB(A) during daytime and ≤ 55 dB(A) at night.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Authority fire safety certificate for site offices, fuel storage, and chemical storage units; structural load inspection certificate for excavation supports and diaphragm wall panels issued by a licensed structural engineer; workplace clearance from the Ministry of Manpower for temporary works, including excavation edge protection, emergency rescue, and personal protective equipment compliance under Law No. 12 of 2003 (Labor Law).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; Unified portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; ELMIS electronic tax registration module: https://elmis.eta.gov.eg; Mandatory e-invoicing clearance platform: https://einvoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity first registers its Egyptian presence (LLC, branch, or project office) with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI), then appoints a tax representative under notarized power of attorney. The unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) is obtained through ETA Form No. 266 filed via ELMIS or at the competent tax office, attaching the GAFI certificate, commercial register excerpt, constitutional documents, and the executed engineering contract for the deep foundation scope. Upon issuance of the tax card, the taxpayer must complete VAT registration when annual taxable turnover exceeds EGP 500,000 or immediately for large contracts, and subsequently onboard to the ETA e-invoicing sandbox to receive digital signing certificates for real-time fiscal clearance of every invoice.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; an Egyptian LLC is statutorily opaque and always taxed at entity level under Law 91 of 2005. Available elections are limited to (i) the presumptive tax regime for micro, small, and medium enterprises under Law 152 of 2020 where annual turnover does not exceed EGP 20 million, (ii) a deemed-profit assessment basis for foreign contractor permanent establishments that keep inadequate books, and (iii) statutory depreciation and foreign tax credit elections. No hybrid-mismatch election is recognized under Egyptian law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) - Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended, and its Executive Regulations, administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover in supplies of goods and services (Article 17/1 of VAT Law 67/2016); a foreign geotechnical contractor performing deep slurry trenching works in Egypt is registrable regardless of turnover because a fixed project site creates a taxable establishment nexus
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time fiscal clearance: every VAT invoice must be generated in certified software, transmitted in XML/JSON to the ETA e-invoicing API (OAuth2-authenticated), validated by the ETA, and returned with a unique UUID and embedded QR code required on the invoice document. B2B and B2C e-invoice/e-receipt mandates apply in phased tranches by taxpayer turnover; un-cleared invoices are legally ineffective, expose the seller to a fine per invoice, and block input VAT deduction and export zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 19(1) of VAT Law 67/2016, goods physically exported from Egypt and services rendered to a non-resident beneficiary and wholly consumed outside Egypt are taxable at 0%. For ISIC 4390 deep trenching and diaphragm wall contracting, zero-rating is available only when the construction site and the benefit of the works are located outside Egypt, or when specialized equipment is exported and title passes to a non-resident principal abroad; works performed on domestic Egyptian sites must be invoiced at 14% standard VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration issued through the NAFEZA single window evidencing physical export
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill proving dispatch and destination outside Egypt
Inward Remittance Certificate from a licensed Egyptian bank confirming receipt of the foreign currency export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to ETA post-clearance audit and electronic reconciliation against the e-invoicing clearance record, customs declarations, and bank FX receipts. If any required document is missing, the export is re-characterized as a domestic taxable supply and the ETA will assess 14% VAT, apply late-payment surcharges at 2% per month from the original VAT return due date, and reverse refunds already paid. Wilful misdeclaration constitutes tax evasion punishable by a fine in the range of 3x to 5x of the evaded tax, imprisonment of the responsible officers, and loss of refund eligibility for a minimum period, with enforced collection via garnishment or lien over project proceeds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — the sole regulatory authority for banking, foreign exchange, and monetary policy under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194 of 2020, its Executive Regulations, and CBE Foreign Exchange Circulars.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian pound (EGP) operates under a managed float with full current-account convertibility for bona fide trade and services through CBE-authorized banks. Capital-account transactions (direct investment, equity injections, intercompany loans) are permitted but require structured documentary compliance, CBE registration, and downstream repatriation approval. Profit remittances by foreign shareholders are generally permissible if the original capital was brought into Egypt through the banking system and the CBE's Foreign Investment Notification was obtained at the time of contribution; settlement of current account payments requires an audited statement of the corporate's EGP income and a tax clearance certificate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: All export receipts (including proceeds from construction services rendered abroad) must be remitted to Egypt through an authorized bank. Under the CBE's March 2024 exchange-rate liberalization, the prior mandatory conversion ratio of 100% of export proceeds to EGP was suspended; the retained foreign currency may be deposited in a domestic foreign-currency account. The exporter must submit an export declaration and provide documentary evidence of the shipment/service within the CBE-prescribed period (generally 5 business days after receipt for services; goods must be credited within the contractual settlement period not exceeding 180 days). Temporary CBE circulars may re-impose a conversion obligation during balance-of-payments stress; such circulars have historically required conversion within 5–15 days of crediting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary treasury rail; offshore digital EMIs cannot hold EGP or directly access local clearing. They may be used for funding flows outside Egypt, but all Egypt-denominated operations must clear through a CBE-authorized bank partner. Licensed local fintechs (e.g., under CBE Fintech Regulations) can provide cross-border collection and payment API rails under a bank sponsorship; viability is Medium for sub-disbursement to subcontractors and low-value vendor payments after the bank validates the fintech's AML framework.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical KYC interview of the LLC's executive director and at least one designated signatory at the branch is effectively mandatory during initial onboarding. CBE's rules permit remote video identification for low-risk and fully-Egyptian-owned entities, but for a foreign-owned LLC, the bank's compliance team will require in-person attendance of the UBO, a second director, and the company secretary; board minutes authorizing signatories must be notarized in the home jurisdiction and legalized by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Partial or opaque UBO structure; ultimate ownership held through a non-Egyptian holding company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBE-compliant UBO declaration, GAFI certificate of incorporation and ownership extract, notarized constitutional documents (AOA/MAA), board resolution on signatories, passport and address proof of each UBO >25%, audited parent-company financials, bank reference letters from the parent's lead bank, and a description of the contractual award mechanism of the construction project.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large milestone payments received in USD from a GCC or EU client under a cross-border construction contract without concurrent export movement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed construction contract, certified progress/work completion certificates, project invoice with a precise valuation narrative, mapping of the payment to the contract milestone schedule, RFP/BOQ documents, and a statement from the contract engineer confirming physical site activity at the diamond-coring and diaphragm-wall work site.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign currency deposits disproportionate to the LLC's registered capital or booked revenue (potential layering indicator).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBE Foreign Investment Notification for equity injections, notarized shareholder loan agreements with amortization/repatriation clauses, audited financial statements and related tax registration, an internally consistent cash-flow projection, and the original deposit ticket with a clear transaction purpose (e.g., bid bond for a new tender, performance guarantee, or mobilization advance).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign equity or subordinated-debt capital must be wired via SWIFT MT202/MT103 to the LLC's capital account at an authorized Egyptian bank, with the remittance advice shown as 'Share Capital Contribution' or 'Non-resident Direct Investment' under the Unified Investment Law No. 72 of 2017. The receiving bank will register the inflow with the CBE and issue a Capital Inflow Registration Certificate; this certificate is the only basis for future profit repatriation or capital liquidation. Contributions exceeding the registered share capital are treated as shareholder loans or as adjustments requiring prior GAFI/CBE approval. The board must adopt a capital-integration resolution and open a temporary CBE-designated foreign-currency account before remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Vendor and sub-contractor disbursements are routed primarily through SWIFT MT103 from the LLC's operational EGP or foreign-currency account. Commercial import payments are supported by the CBE's ACI platform (Advance Cargo Information) and are settled via an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (UCP600) with a 20–30% cash cover (depending on the bank's limit confinement) or, for smaller transactions, by telegraphic transfer after invoice verification. Standby LCs and demand guarantees for performance bonds are issued against cash collateral or reduced exposure limits under the bank's corporate facility; the bank will approve the LC amount only after the tender/project contract is reviewed and the CBE's import/forfeiting rules are satisfied.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EGP deliverable currency forwards with CBE-authorized dealing banks, tenors up to 12 months, for covering contracted import obligations.
Egyptian-pound non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for cross-border counterparties, only with CBE-approved banks and under a documented underlying trade exposure.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP) for hedging the US-dollar-denominated debt or receivables of the LLC, subject to CBE ring-fencing rules and representative limits.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general CIT holiday for the EG_LLC. Preferential treatment derives from Investment Law No. 72 of 2017: 50% investment-cost deduction for expansion projects in underdeveloped governorates; Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) / Free Zone profit streams may be subject to a 1%-2% annual fee in lieu of CIT; 'Golden License' projects receive consolidated approvals and customs relief. The deep-foundation contracting activity (ISIC 4390) qualifies only where the assets and workforce are physically deployed in Egypt.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (ETA Model 41) filed through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) unified electronic declaration and e-filing portal (eta.gov.eg). The TP declaration annex (Form 3 / TP Disclosure) is attached electronically when controlled transactions exist.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing within four months after the close of the fiscal year (by 30 April for a calendar-year taxpayer). The ETA may allow a short extension in practice; the 2%-per-month late-payment surcharge keeps accruing even where an extension is granted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: LLC name, tax card (bitaqa dharibeya) number, economic registration number, fiscal year-end, ISIC activity code (4390), and the legal representative signing the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident with a PE in Egypt: use the PE registration details and state the head-office jurisdiction and branch status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All taxable gross revenue, including milestone billings, mobilization/demobilization payments, variation orders, and claims collected from the deep slurry trenching and diaphragm wall contracts. Reconciliation with e-invoices (Dar Al-Iftaa? no) issued.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: enter only Egyptian-source gross revenue attributable to the PE; backup with signed contracts and bank confirmations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Subcontractor costs, bentonite/cement/steel-bar materials, plant and equipment depreciation, site labor, insurance, financing costs (subject to thin cap 4:1), and general overheads. Deductions require e-invoices, bank transfer evidence, and delivery/consumption records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: deduct only expenses economically borne by the PE and substantiated in Egypt; head-office cost allocations need TP conformity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs for disallowed entertainment, penalties paid, concealed drawings, non-deductible provisions, and 20% of unsubstantiated cash disbursements; subtract exempt income and investment incentives under Law 72/2017.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: adjustments follow the same Egyptian statutory items; no foreign head-office losses may be set off.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct prior-year tax losses only within the 5-year carry-forward window and under continuity of ownership/activity conditions. Any unused losses expire at year five.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE: only losses previously computed for the Egyptian PE are available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 22.5% corporate rate to the taxable base; deduct the foreign tax credit (unilateral or under DTA), any investment/profit-retention credits, advance CIT instalments already paid, and self-assess the final balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident: request refunds of excess Egyptian WHT through the treaty relief or claim process within the statutory limitation period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed statutory fine plus an additional monthly surcharge of 2% of the assessed tax (accumulating per month of delay, capped at 100% of the tax). Non-filing triggers an ETA best-of-judgment (deemed) assessment, loss of the right to use loss carry-forwards, and criminal referral against the legal representative for deliberate concealment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To reduce the 10% domestic dividend WHT, the non-resident beneficial owner must (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority for the calendar year of the distribution, (ii) complete the ETA-prescribed treaty relief/beneficial-ownership declaration, and (iii) deliver the certified TRC to the Egyptian distributing company before the dividend payment. Relief at source is applied if the payer accepts the documents; otherwise the non-resident files a refund claim with the ETA within the five-year prescription window. The intermediary LLC must avoid shell-company characterization to retain treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT: 20% on interest and 20% on royalties/licence fees paid to non-residents without a PE; same 20% applies to technical and management service bills that are recharacterized as royalties. Dividend distributors pay 10%. Treaties cap rates (e.g., China-Egypt DTA: dividends 8%/20% split, interest and royalties capped at 10%; most European and Gulf DTAs: 10%-20%). Relief requires the TRC and beneficial-ownership evidence.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a Gulf-style standalone ESR regime, but Law No. 91 of 2005 (Arts. 27 and 68) and the executive regulations apply substance-over-form, GAAR, beneficial-ownership tests, a 4:1 thin-capitalization limit on interest, and CFC-type attribution for offshore passive income. The ETA may disregard an artificial intermediate entity, impute the contractor's profits, and deny DTA relief where the EG_LLC fails to demonstrate actual site personnel, equipment, contracts, and decision-making in Egypt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - False or Deficient CIT Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating deep-foundation contract billings, using forged supplier invoices, maintaining parallel cash ledgers for variation orders, or destroying accounting records to avoid ETA assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Law No. 91 of 2005 (Arts. 133-135) and the Unified Tax Procedures Law No. 206 of 2020: imprisonment of 6 months to 5 years and a fine not exceeding twice the evaded tax, with the unpaid tax and the 2%-per-month surcharge (capped at 100%) collected in full.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director signing the return is jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax if willful concealment is proven; the ETA may impose travel bans, freeze bank accounts, and secure asset attachments against the director and the LLC. Corporate-veil piercing under the Egyptian Civil Code (Art. 55) applies where the LLC is operated as the shareholders' alter ego.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Profit Stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing equipment rental, geotechnical engineering fees, or group personnel costs through non-arm's-length related suppliers; persistent low margins; failure to file the TP annex or Local File once controlled transactions exceed EGP 5,000,000; absence of contemporaneous benchmarking.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA re-computation of the taxable margin under best-judgment principles, disallowance of the mispriced deductions, and a 2%-per-month delayed-payment surcharge on the resulting deficiency. Document failure exposes the taxpayer to fixed TP fines and the loss of the right to adjust the return by audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve and sign the TP declaration face criminal fines where false statements are certified; deliberate intercompany fraud supports evasion charges and personal indemnification, while the ETA can enjoin the director's travel pending the TP audit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inserting a tax-haven or DTA-jurisdiction entity with no employees, equipment, or project control to invoice diaphragm-wall consulting and engineering fees from Egypt, or distributing profits to a nominee shareholder to disguise the true beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the artificial entity under GAAR/substance-over-form, re-attribution of the whole contract profit to the EG_LLC, denial of the DTA rate (back to the statutory 20% royalty/interest or 10% dividend WHT), and penalties of up to 200% of the under-withheld tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The veil is pierced: founders and directors become jointly liable for the reassessed tax; the ETA may issue an asset freeze and a travel ban; criminal referral follows when the sham arrangement was used to launder project proceeds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting milestone cash payments or paying subcontractors in cash above the statutory reporting/threshold limits, omitting beneficial-ownership declarations, transferring funds without bank documentary evidence (contravening the banking-channel deductibility rules), or contracting with sanctioned parties for imported construction equipment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under AML Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended): fines from EGP 100,000 to EGP 1,000,000 and imprisonment from 6 months to 3 years for non-reported transfers and false beneficial-ownership filings; the ETA also disallows unbanked cash expenses from the CIT computation, raising the 22.5% effective burden.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers and directors who authorize cash schemes are personally prosecuted; funds used in the violation are confiscated; travel bans and passport holds apply pending the money-laundering investigation; the individual penalty accompanies the corporate fine, leaving directors personally exposed notwithstanding the LLC's limited liability.
